rules.summary: Stetson's policy says an athlete may use their NIL to promote business activities as long as the athlete gets no pay in exchange for athletics participation or achievements.
rules.conditions: The policy was last revised September 16, 2025. Stetson later announced it opts in to the House settlement from 2026-27. The policy text was not changed to mention direct school payments.
rules.citation: Stetson Name, Image, and Likeness Policy v.5, Policy
rules.short_answer: No pay for playing or for results.

sources.quote: so long as the student-athlete does not receive any compensation in exchange for their athletics participation or achievements

rules.summary: Stetson's policy says an athlete may use their name, image and likeness to promote athletic and non-athletic business activities. It gives products, services, camps and clinics, and personal appearances as examples.
rules.citation: Stetson Name, Image, and Likeness Policy v.5, Policy

sources.quote: may use their name, image, and likeness (“NIL”) to promote their athletically and non-athletically related business activities (e.g., products, services, camps & clinics, personal appearances)
Earning compensation from their NIL itself will not affect a student-athletes grant-in-aid or athletic eligibility.

rules.summary: Stetson's policy says NIL pay must be for a valid business purpose. It says rates and terms must match what similar people with similar NIL value are paid.
rules.citation: Stetson Name, Image, and Likeness Policy v.5, Policy
rules.short_answer: Pay must match a real business purpose and market rates.

sources.quote: such compensation is for a valid business purpose with compensation at rates and terms commensurate with compensation paid to similarly situated individuals with comparable name, image and likeness value

rules.summary: Stetson's policy says an athlete's business promotion may mention their role in college sports and may mention Stetson University. If they do, they must add a disclaimer that the views or services are theirs alone.

rules.short_answer: Yes, with an 'opinions are my own' style disclaimer.

sources.quote: A student-athlete’s promotion of a business activity may include a reference to the student-athlete’s involvement in intercollegiate athletics and a reference to Stetson University.
they must include a disclaimer that the views expressed or services provided are theirs alone and not those of Stetson University or Stetson University Athletics

rules.summary: Stetson's policy says any use of Stetson's name, marks or symbols must follow Stetson Athletics' Branding and Style Guides. The 2023 athletics brand guide says use of the logos without consent is prohibited.

rules.summary: Stetson's policy says athletes cannot sign a deal that ties the university name or marks to products or services that compete with Stetson Athletics' exclusive sponsors. rules.conditions: The policy does not list product categories such as gambling, alcohol or tobacco.
rules.citation: Stetson Name, Image, and Likeness Policy v.5, Policy
rules.short_answer: No deals that pair Stetson's name or marks with a rival of an exclusive sponsor.

student-athletes should not enter into contract or transactions that violate NCAA legislation, Stetson University policies, Federal or State Laws; or reflect negatively on Stetson University and/or the Stetson University Athletics program.

rules.short_answer: Stetson may sign NIL license or endorsement deals with athletes.

rules.summary: Stetson's policy says an athlete must disclose NIL contracts or transactions to NIL GO. Deals from non-school payors worth $600 or more in total must be reported, with written documentation, within five business days of signing.
rules.conditions: The $600 total counts multiple deals or payments from the same or substantially the same third party, including affiliates. Athletes also attest on NIL GO registration that all such deals will be reported.
rules.citation: Stetson Name, Image, and Likeness Policy v.5, Policy (page 3) and Procedures (page 5)
rules.short_answer: Report to NIL GO within five business days. $600 total is the threshold.

with a total value of $600 or more to the designated name, image and likeness clearinghouse for review.

such activities must be reported if the aggregate value is $600 or more during the student-athlete’s period of eligibility.

sources.quote: NIL GO will review the proposed contract or transaction for compliance with NCAA rules.

rules.summary: Stetson's policy says an athlete who misses the five business day deadline should get a reasonable time to disclose. After that, Stetson should withhold institutional assistance and services until the athlete discloses.

sources.quote: After the reasonable time to cure the failure to disclose has lapsed, Stetson University should withhold institutional assistance and services until the student-athlete discloses the relevant NIL activities.

provided the entity that will use the student- athlete’s name, image and likeness rights for the promotion or endorsement of its goods or services provided to the general public for profit is the originating source of the compensation

sources.quote: Stetson University will provide annual financial literacy, life skills, and entrepreneurship workshops for student-athletes.

notes: Pages read in full: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 and 6. All text was read by eye from screenshots (read_method visual), so a human should spot check quotes against the viewer. Quotes keep the on-screen wording, including 'student- athlete’s' and 'a student-athletes grant-in-aid'.

The Purpose section still says the policy ensures compliance with 'current NCAA interim policies and Florida state legislation', and the Policy section cites Section 1006.74, Florida Statute. The policy does not use the words House settlement or revenue sharing.

The policy bars pay 'in exchange for their athletics participation or achievements'. Stetson's December 18, 2025 release says it opts in to the House settlement from 2026-27. The policy text has not been revised since September 16, 2025.

Not addressed in the policy: boosters (only 'associated entities or individuals' in the $600 reporting sentence), collectives, uniforms, team-issued gear, product categories such as gambling or alcohol, and any penalty beyond withholding institutional assistance and services.

Frequency of Review: the policy says it is reviewed every three years, or sooner when conference, NCAA, Florida or federal rules change.

The logos and wordmarks are the official marks of Bethune-Cookman University, and only those with permission to use the marks may do so.
